decisions.reason: The one-video source constraint does not change the substantive lesson-value standard; message 84 already independently modifies that standard through a separate explicit clause.
Requiring all eight clips to come from one video does not alter narrative completeness; message 84 already independently refines completeness through a separate explicit clause.
The source-selection change neither modifies nor removes the existing good-hook criterion.
Selecting all eight clips from one video does not change the existing 20-to-120-second duration limits.
The one-video source constraint does not change visual-editing rules; message 84 already independently modifies those rules through its clean, simple, professional editing clause.
The candidate already requires an eight-clip trial batch before message 84; the new one-video constraint affects source selection rather than batch count or delivery work.
The source-selection decision does not change the existing caption color treatment.
The candidate already specifies 180 approved clips per month, and the trial's one-video source constraint does not alter that ongoing production target.
The source-selection change has no necessary effect on caption font selection or its prior runtime verification.
